MALARIA 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
SIGNS & SYMPTOMS 
 
* Fever  
* Arthralgia 
* Fatigue 
* Myalgia 
* Malaise 
* Abdominal pain 
* Anorexia 
* Vomiting 
* Headache 
* Dizziness 
* Cough * Rigors 
* Travel history 
HIGH RISK GROUPS 
 
* Children 
* Pregnant & postpartum 
* Elderly > 65 years 
* HIV 
* Previous splenectomy 
* Travel history to a malaria area 
GENERAL MANAGEMENT 
 
* ABC approach 
 
- Shock Balsol/Ringers Lactate 20ml/kg bolus 
* Blood Glucose, Hb & U-dipstix 
* BLOODS: FBC, U&E, CRP, Malaria smear & antigen 
* Antipyretics 
 
* If smear or antigen positive, start appropriate  
   anti-malarial therapy 
 
UNCOMPLICATED MALARIA 
 
* Mild symptoms 
* Ambulant 
* No end organ dysfunction 
* < 5% parasitaemia 
 
Antimalarial Therapy 
 
* Co-artemÒ: 
 
4 tablets STAT, 4 after 8 hours. Then BD for 2 days 
 
If Co-artemÒ is unavailable 
* Quinine plus Doxycycline 
* Pregnancy/Children à Quinine plus Clindamycin 
 
* Quinine 
 
 
- Start on day 1 
 
- 10mg/kg po TDS x 7 days  
* Doxycycline 
 
- Start on day 2 
 
- 3.5mg/kg OD x 7 days 
* Clindamycin 
 
- Start on day 2 
 
- Children: 
3-6mg/kg OD x 7 days  
 
- Adults:  
300mg po BD x 7 days  
 
Note: 
Observe for vomiting for 1 hour in the ED. If no vomiting à discharge 
If vomiting occurs within 1 hour, re-administer dose & observe. 
If vomiting persists à Refer to Infectious Diseases (ID) 
ADMISSION CRITERIA 
 
* Persistent vomiting 
* Pregnant women 
* Age > 65 years 
* Patients with co-morbidities 
DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS 
 
* Malaria is a NOTIFIABLE DISEASE 
* Paracetamol if required 
* Advise adequate fluid intake 
* Clinical response occurs within 24-48 hours 
* Refer to local clinic for follow up 
* Advise about worsening symptoms 
Dr R Gihwala CMJAH Emergency Department June 2020 
Contents

COMPLICATED MALARIA 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
DEFINING CRITERIA FOR SEVERE MALARIA 
(Any one or combinations of the following criteria applies) 
 
Clinical Features 
 
* Impaired consciousness or unarousable coma 
* Convulsions: > 2 episodes in 24 hours 
* Respiratory distress, acidotic breathing, pulmonary oedema 
* Circulatory collapse / Shock:  SBP < 70 mmHg in adults; SBP < 50 mmHg in children  
* Jaundice 
* Bleeding 
* Prostration 
 
Laboratory Findings 
 
* Hypoglycaemia: blood glucose < 2.2 mmol/L 
* Acidosis: serum lactate > 5 mmol/L  or  plasma bicarbonate < 15 mmol/L 
* Hepatic transaminases > 3 times normal 
* Renal impairment: Creatinine > 265 µmol/L or rapidly rising creatinine or                        
                                     urine output < 400 mL/day in adults 
* Haemoglobin < 5 g/dL 
* Parasitaemia ³ 5% 
* ³ 5% neutrophils contain malaria pigment 
* Presence of schizonts of P. falciparum in peripheral blood smear 
IMMEDIATE ASSESSMENT & MANAGEMENT 
 
* ABC approach to resuscitation 
* Monitors 
* Large bore IV line
